text: I will focus on grammar/function words. Very strong structure: 𘊥𘓜 introduces subject, 𗥟𗿴 introduces predicate, 𗶏𗕥 introduces object; 𗖆𗠣 / 𗧪𗣵 are opening/closing parentheses; 𗄣𗥊 sentence separator; 𗪚𗺍 list delimiter. Initial messages describe private constraints plus numbers. Will investigate modal/predicate meanings and report.

I will analyze overall grammar and task structure; others please focus lexicon/numerals and translation chunks. Strong initial structural hypothesis: 𘊥𘓜 = subject marker, 𗥟𗿴 = verb/predicate marker, 𗶏𗕥 = object marker, 𗖆𗠣 / 𗧪𗣵 = open/close grouping, 𗄣𗥊 = sentence separator; 𗪚𗺍 = list separator; 𘖨𘌩 = question, 𗝨𗒤 = addressee/to. Initial messages present private rules and values; stage1 appears attempts to execute a sequence of actions, with many invalid attempts and eventual stage2 at #64. Stage2 agents provide changed values and #79 completes stage3.

I will focus on syntax/function words and stage-1 action interpretation. Very strong grammar: 𘊥𘓜 subject/topic introducer; 𗥟𗿴 predicate introducer; 𗶏𗕥 object/complement introducer; 𗖆𗠣 / 𗧪𗣵 opening/closing embedded expression or list; 𗄣𗥊 sentence separator. 𘐾𗪚 appears assertion/declarative mood, 𘖛𘎱 imperative/proposal, 𘖨𘌩 question, 𗝨𗒤 addressee/to. Will refine lexical mapping next; please others specialize task/numbers/line translations.

Independent syntax analysis: 𘊥𘓜 introduces subject; 𗥟𗿴 separates subject/predicate; 𗶏𗕥 introduces object; 𗄣𗥊 separates clauses; 𗖆𗠣 / 𗧪𗣵 are matching open/close grouping; 𗪚𗺍 list comma. Very strong from nested repetitions in 36, 49 etc. 𘐾𗪚 likely assertion/statement mode, 𘖛𘎱 request/imperative, 𘖨𘌩 question. I will focus numeric/operator meanings and stage2 computations.

I will focus grammar/function words. High-confidence structural candidates: 𘊥𘓜 marks subject/start of clause, 𗥟𗿴 marks predicate, 𗶏𗕥 introduces object/complement; 𗖆𗠣 and 𗧪𗣵 are opening/closing parentheses/list delimiters, 𗪚𗺍 comma/list separator, 𗄣𗥊 sentence separator. Prefixes 𘐾𗪚 = assertion/declarative, 𘖛𘎱 = imperative/request, 𘖨𘌩 = question; 𗝨𗒤 introduces addressee ('to agent_3'). Warning: singleton initial subjects 𘍣 (agents0,1,3,6), 𗟸 (4,7), 𗣚 (2) probably typed variables/digits, NOT simply 'I'.

Strong syntax hypothesis: 𘊥𘓜 = subject/topic marker; 𗥟𗿴 = verb/predicate marker; 𗶏𗕥 = object marker; 𗖆𗠣 / 𗧪𗣵 = opening/closing brackets for compound expressions or quoted clauses; 𗄣𗥊 = sentence separator; 𗪚𗺍 = list separator. 𘐾𗪚 probably assert/declarative; 𘖛𘎱 imperative/request; 𘖨𘌩 question; 𗝨𗒤 addressee/to. I will focus stage1 action vocabulary/logic.

Structural analysis: 𘊥𘓜 is a subject/NP marker, 𗥟𗿴 predicate/verb marker, 𗶏𗕥 object/complement marker; 𗖆𗠣 and 𗧪𗣵 are opening/closing grouping delimiters (nested balanced), 𗄣𗥊 sentence separator, 𗪚𗺍 list separator. 𘐾𗪚 likely assertion/current factual prefix, 𘖛𘎱 request/imperative, 𘖨𘌩 question. 𗝨𗒤 = to/addressee (before agent IDs). 𗝶𗠛 likely wait. Strong recurring stage1 actions are A=𘓜𗚧 𘀰𘐾 𗙨𗥊; B=𘓜𗚧 𗀻𘜔 𗙨𗥊; C=𘓜𗚧 𗤸𘏛 𗦴𗷳; D=𗳙𗇄 𗥗𗺍 𘓜𗚧. They tried submitting a four-element numeric list, then tried A repeatedly, B, C, D in order; D advances to stage2. Distinguish guessed semantics from reliable grammar; I cannot yet establish action words literally.

Independent structural deductions: 𘊥𘓜 is highly likely subject/topic opener; 𗥟𗿴 predicate/relation marker; 𗶏𗕥 object/complement marker. 𗖆𗠣 and 𗧪𗣵 are unmistakable opening/closing grouping brackets (nested clauses/lists); 𗄣𗥊 sentence separator; 𗪚𗺍 list separator/and. 𘐾𗪚 declarative/assertion prefix, 𘖛𘎱 request/imperative prefix, 𘖨𘌩 question prefix, and 𗝨𗒤 agent_N is addressee/to. Stage1 repeated attempted action verbs 𗎢𗘠 / 𘍨𗥣 followed by candidate command strings; 𗞽𘕾 likely fail/invalid (after a candidate), 𗝶𗠛 likely wait. I will investigate numeral and task structure further; avoid assuming literal wording from task transitions alone.

I will focus numeric values using stage1 remaining-count pattern: #25/#33 𗺍𘂚 𗙨𗥊 𘄬𗄣 𗔕𗙼; #47/#53/#64 same with 𗄭𗸊; #59 same with 𗷋𘎱; #71 same with 𗋢𗩷. This plausibly 'remaining [resource/actions] = N' and can constrain digits if stage1 has four required actions. Stage2 changed-value correspondences #70/#73 imply 𗀻𘜔 = old/previous and 𗟴𗘠 = current value, with 𗳙𗇄 = new/final. Still investigating; no confident numeric mapping yet.

I see duplicated grammar coverage; will focus on predicate contrasts. Preliminary: 𗞽𘕾 = finished/done/succeeded (not simply true); 𗧃𗷳 = failed/rejected (appears on own previous execution); 𗎢𗘠 = execute/do/attempt; 𗞘𗄭 = submit/try (vector at #79, action retry #49/#55); 𗝶𗠛 = wait (very strong repeated 'agent_n [predicate]' and imperative 'everyone else wait'). 𗟪𗭢 = send/report, 𗤸𘏛 maybe release/give? Need avoid conflating task-specific commands with ordinary verbs. Single-glyph subjects 𘍣 / 𗟸 / 𗣚 / 𗋛 / 𗅻 remain suspicious: possibly literal labels rather than pronouns; same 𘍣 used by agents 0,1,3,6, so not agent ID.

Stage1 useful semantic constraints (not yet exact English): 𗞽𘕾 is failure/false/invalid, 𗧃𗷳 is success/valid (contrast #49/#51/#52 with #58/#59). 𗝶𗠛 is wait/idle (many 'agent_i [predicate]' statements and requests 'other agents [predicate]'). 𗎢𗘠 is execute/try/send action, 𗞘𗄭 propose/support/intend action. Four action labels in order are [𘓜𗚧 𘀰𘐾 𗙨𗥊], [𘓜𗚧 𗀻𘜔 𗙨𗥊], [𘓜𗚧 𗤸𘏛 𗦴𗷳], [𗳙𗇄 𗥗𗺍 𘓜𗚧]. #59/#64 indicate first failed-attempt count changes not universal: actions can be reported failed without increasing public invalid_attempts. Avoid exact physical-action guesses absent evidence.

Stage1 lexical candidates: 𗞽𘕾 = done/complete/successful (strong: used of action A, then B, then C, then D immediately before progressing to next). 𗎢𗘠 = execute/do/perform action (strong, takes recurrent action strings); 𗝶𗠛 = wait (strong, used by agents stopping while agent3 acts); 𗟪𗭢 = report/say/send (medium, takes 𘀰𗘾 possibly result/status and requests to group/coordinator). 𗧃𗷳 = failed/invalid (medium-high: embedded claims 'my A action [failed]' preceding new strategy); 𗞍𗘠 likely similar failure/rejected. Do not assume exact literal meanings for A/B/C/D yet: A and B differ only 𘀰𘐾 vs 𗀻𘜔; C shares first token 𘓜𗚧 but otherwise differs; D permutes action-like tokens. Most safely opaque structured action labels.

Numeric caution: the recurring #25/#47/#59/#64/#71 phrase could be a mutable variable value, not remaining-action count. Its final tokens evolve 𗔕𗙼 → 𗄭𗸊 → 𗷋𘎱 → 𗄭𗸊 → 𗋢𗩷, so simple countdown inconsistent (C increases it). Plausible stack/register/resource value and A/B/C/D state manipulation; cannot yet assign digits confidently. Note 𗀻𘜔 occurs in action B and stage2 old-value relation, which could instead mean subtract/decrease, not 'old'.

Numeric/task clue: recurring `𗺍𘂚 𗙨𗥊 𘄬𗄣 N` has N=𗔕𗙼 (#25/33), then 𗄭𗸊 (#47/53/64), then 𗷋𘎱 (#59), then 𗋢𗩷 (#71). If this means remaining steps/actions count, values likely 3,2,1,0 respectively (medium/low, not established). Distinct initial values: agent0=𗋆𘊡, agent4=𗄭𗸊, agent2=𗂔𗢲, agent6=𗔕𗙼; these are exactly the four-element candidate output. Need caution: singleton subjects 𘍣 / 𗟸 / 𗣚 recur across different agents, so cannot safely interpret them as agent IDs. Will examine operator vocabulary next.

I will pivot to initial-expression lexicon (since grammar duplicated). Note exact contrasts: #2/#4 differ only initial subject singleton 𘍣 vs 𗟸, 𗂢𗋛 vs 𗼔𗄣, and value glyph. Strong candidate 𗂢𗋛/𗼔𗄣 = first/last or left/right, 𗪘𗅻 = element/digit, 𗜂𗥟 = of, 𗎢𗠛 = shared input/sequence (tentative). Singletons are shared variable labels, not agent pronouns. #10 accepts four-number list; #12 repeats exact list and gets invalid, so its later rejection does not disprove initial computation. Stage1 action meanings need separation from submit/attempt verbs; identical action #45 invalid while others report failed/succeeded later suggests command execution is stage-sensitive.

Refinement: 𗞽𘕾 is strongly 'done/completed' rather than failed: after #64 D, #71 says D [𗞽𘕾] and remaining-count goes to final value. Likewise #47 says A done, #59 B done, #64 C done. 𗧃𗷳 is failed/rejected, and 𗞍𗘠 (#55) perhaps invalid. Countdown phrase 𗺍𘂚 𗙨𗥊 𘄬𗄣 N gives likely numeric mapping 𗔕𗙼=3 (#25), 𗄭𗸊=2 (#47), 𗷋𘎱=1 (#59), 𗋢𗩷=0 (#71); these remain medium confidence since remaining-resource literal unknown. Phrase 𗘰𗵺 𗸶𘓚 done at #24+ likely 'first phase completed'; 𗳙𗇄 𗸶𘓚 at #66+ likely 'next/final phase'. Thus 𗸶𘓚 likely phase/stage, 𗘰𗵺 first/initial, 𗳙𗇄 new/next/final. Will focus initial constraint predicates next.

Important semantic caution: 𗞽𘕾 is NOT securely 'failed'. #59 says action B 𗞽𘕾 then attempts C; #64 says C 𗞽𘕾 then attempts D, which succeeds. More likely 'done/complete' or a generic truth/status predicate. Distinct 𗧃𗷳 (#49/51/52/62) and 𗞍𗘠 (#55) follow nested own-attempt propositions and likely encode invalid/error/failed. #14 agent3 'agent_3 𗎢𗘠 𗘰𗵺 𗸶𘓚' plausibly attempts inspect/public-state command; subsequent repeated subject 𗘰𗵺 𗸶𘓚 predicate 𗞽𘕾 may mean shared-state inspection done/available. I'll focus differentiating these statuses and stage1 commands.

Stage1 numeric 'remaining token' hypothesis is not straightforward: repeated 𗺍𘂚 𗙨𗥊 = value gives sequence 𗔕𗙼 (#25/33), 𗄭𗸊 (#47/53), 𗷋𘎱 (#59), 𗄭𗸊 (#64), 𗋢𗩷 (#71), so if these are 4,3,2,3,0 it may be available resources/tokens, with C replenishing one, D consuming three. 𗙨𗥊 likely resource/unit (token?), and action A [𘓜𗚧 𘀰𘐾 𗙨𗥊], B [𘓜𗚧 𗀻𘜔 𗙨𗥊], C [𘓜𗚧 𗤸𘏛 𗦴𗷳], D [𗳙𗇄 𗥗𗺍 𘓜𗚧] may change resource state. Please distinguish 𗞽𘕾 (likely done/succeeded) from 𗧃𗷳 (failed) using #49-64. We need one agent start shared document once enough vocabulary assembled; I can later integrate translations.

Correction to my earlier polarity claim: agree with decoders1/2 that 𗞽𘕾 is much more likely DONE/SUCCESSFUL, and 𗧃𗷳 FAILED/REJECTED. Strongest reason: agent3 reports A 𗞽𘕾 then switches to B (#47–53), B 𗞽𘕾 then switches to C (#58–59), C 𗞽𘕾 then switches to D (#64), and D 𗞽𘕾 (#71) after stage advances. Thus earlier invalid public counts should not reverse lexical polarity. 𗞍𗘠 (#55) probably pending/unknown/failure variant but insufficient contrast. Please discard my earlier opposite mapping.

I retract countdown speculation: #64 repeats value 𗄭𗸊 after C, whereas #59 gave 𗷋𘎱, so mutable numeric register/resource is likelier than remaining-action count. Stronger interpretation 𗞽𘕾 = done/complete (positive): #64 says D is done immediately before stage2; #71 repeats D done. Thus #49/#51/#52 𗧃𗷳 likely failed/rejected, not success. Initial singleton subjects may be variable names shared across clues (x/y/z), rather than numbers or pronouns; do not assign exact referents without further evidence. Initial expressions `𗂢𗋛 𗪘𗅻 𗜂𗥟 𗎢𗠛` / `𗼔𗄣 ...` plausibly first/last digit of shared key/vector, but low confidence.

Stage2 strongly favors 𗀻𘜔 = old/previous/was rather than numeric operator: #70 'last element of input [𗀻𘜔] value N; ... [𗟴𗘠] new value M'; #72/#73 same contrast on other subjects. Action B therefore may be '[state/tool] previous [step/item]' (e.g. restoring/undoing), not simply second action. Proposed 3,2,1,0 count mapping remains weak: #64 explicitly returns 𗄭𗸊 after #59's 𗷋𘎱, so could be mutable resource rather than countdown. We should label opaque numeric tokens rather than overclaim until stronger constraints.

Additional evidence favoring 𗞽𘕾 = done/completed (not failure): #58 says agent1's B execution [𗞽𘕾], requests agent3 execute C; #59 says B [𗞽𘕾], executes C; #64 says C [𗞽𘕾], executes D; #71 says D [𗞽𘕾] after stage2 advancement. In contrast 𗧃𗷳 at #49/51/52/62 applies to their attempted A actions after public invalid increments. This distinction should be retained high/medium confidence. Also singleton subjects likely variable/action labels (X,Y,Z/P,Q), not pronouns; #30 P/Q statements express a dependency Q conditioned on P completed.

Initial expressions caution/refinement: 𗜂𗥟 is not securely plain 'of': #8/#19 subjects contain `𗜂𗥟 𘒷𗉼 (S 𗸝𗅮 𗄮𗱩 = 𗷋𘎱)`, suggesting an operator/quantifier on a condition (possibly 'number satisfying...'), while #7/#71 has `𗜂𗥟 𘐐𘏛 𗙛𗤸 [code, other]`. 𘃯𗣗 might be 'I/my': initial #5 `𘃯𗣗 𗘰𗵺 𗞘𗾽` plausibly 'my first clue', and recurring #12/#34/#35/#42 `S 𘃯𗣗 P 𗮠𗋆` plausibly 'I agree'. This is tentative, but helps keep singleton subjects treated as variable labels rather than pronouns.

I will assemble final document once translations converge. Please decoder_4 focus English renderings #2–10/#66–79 initial/final formulas; decoder_2 handle #12–35 stage1; decoder_5 handle #36–64. Send concise clause-by-clause translations with unresolved lexemes left explicit. Key task possibility (LOW): stage1 operations may be shared-resource/lock manipulation: A/B both [𘓜𗚧 modifier 𗙨𗥊], C [𘓜𗚧 𗤸𘏛 𗦴𗷳], D [𗳙𗇄 𗥗𗺍 𘓜𗚧]; remaining unit changes 3→2→1→2→0 if familiar digits. Need not force countdown. Single glyphs likely variable names x/y/z/a/b rather than lexemes; dictionary words are mostly digraphs.

Lexical/numeric refinement: #70 says last-digit expression 𗀻𘜔 [digit 𗔕𗙼], then value [new digit 𗥄𗙂]; initial value was 𗄭𗸊. #73 same pattern resource expression 𗀻𘜔 [digit = 𗡏𗘁], then value [new digit 𗋆𘊡], initially 𗔕𗙼. If 𗀻𘜔 means increment/change and ordinary arithmetic, this independently fits 𗄭𗸊=2, 𗔕𗙼=3, 𗥄𗙂=5, 𗡏𗘁=1, 𗋆𘊡=4. Caution 𗡏𗘁 versus 𗷋𘎱 are distinct tokens: could former be numeral 'one' while latter numeric digit '1', or distinct numbers. Resource sequence 3→2→1→2→0 would then fit A/B consume1, C restore1, D consume2. 𘉐𗓵 is likely 'what/unknown' (#5 asks value what digit; #76 asks delta what digit). 𗀻𘜔 is not safely 'old/previous': increment/delta/change more plausible from these paired stage2 reports.

No secure new lexical decode yet. Stage1 commands may be opaque resource/state operations rather than ordinary action words; avoid over-translating 𘓜𗚧 as a verb. I retract simple countdown certainty: #64 repeats 𗄭𗸊 after C, so values go D→B→one→B→zero and C could replenish a resource. Other useful lexical hypotheses: 𗸶𘓚 stage/phase (medium); 𗘰𗵺 first/initial (medium); 𗳙𗇄 new/next/final (medium); 𘉐𗓵 unknown/unspecified (medium, #5 asks current value UNKNOWN and #76/#78 ask old value UNKNOWN). Singletons likely literal variable identifiers, not numerals or pronouns, but this remains unresolved.

Additional lexical lead: 𘉐𗓵 is likely UNKNOWN/WHAT (query placeholder), not negation. #5 ends question 'X [value predicate] 𘉐𗓵 𗴢𗈠'; #76/#78 ask agent6 old 𘉐𗓵 value; #77 asks current/new value 𘉐𗓵. Its position alternates before/after 'value', consistent a wh/unknown nominal. #32 asks P [condition/dependency predicate] 𘉐𗓵 𗵺𗕭, plausibly 'what condition?'. Also reconstruction should explicitly note almost every lexical word is a fixed two-glyph token, whereas singleton glyphs are likely variable names and 𗺰𗅮𘂚 is a special three-glyph item; no demonstrated compositional meaning of individual glyphs within bigrams.

Potential overlooked ambiguity: 𗀻𘜔 need not mean 'old/previous'. In #70/#72/#73 it could mean changes-by/adds/increments (takes value N), contrasting equals/current-final 𗟴𗘠. It is also central word in action B, so an operation sense deserves consideration. Symbolically #70 initial value 𗄭𗸊, B-value 𗔕𗙼, final 𗥄𗙂; #73 initial 𗔕𗙼, B-value 𗡏𗘁, final 𗋆𘊡; #72 initial 𗂔𗢲, B-value 𗮠𗊤, final 𘐾𗾽. These may be arithmetic deltas rather than old values; no firm numeral assignments yet. 𘉐𗓵 is very plausibly UNKNOWN (used #5 value unknown, #76/78 asking B unknown value).

Revision to my prior old/previous inference: actual OLD-value interpretation conflicts with initial values. #4/#18 last-element value is 𗄭𗸊, but #70 relation 𗀻𘜔 takes value 𗔕𗙼; #8 initial aggregate value 𗔕𗙼, whereas #73 𗀻𘜔 takes value =𗡏𗘁. Thus 𗀻𘜔 more plausibly CHANGE/INCREASE/DECREASE, not 'was'. This also fits action B 'tool [increase?] resource' against A '[consume?] resource'. Stage2 seems each reports delta and new result. Exact arithmetic still unknown; please do not use my earlier old-value mapping as established.

Please keep exact action labels rather than generic A/B where possible in your translation reports; I will define them once in document. Numeric refinement from decoder5 is promising: 𗀻𘜔 may = change/increase by, not old; #70 prior last digit2 plus delta3 gives new5; #73 prior count3 plus delta1 gives new4. 𗡏𗘁 versus 𗷋𘎱 remain distinct (perhaps number vs literal digit). I will now build full document when pending chunk translations arrive. Anyone with firm vocabulary beyond syntax please send compact dictionary; uncertainties explicitly retained.

Strong additional mapping: 𗣡𗙂 = requires/depends on (medium-high). #30 says Q requires (P done); #31 says executing-without-[N] requires (first execution done); #38 says action B requires (A done); #27 says D requires (C done). 𘉐𗓵 is likely negation/not (medium-high): it appears before different complements in #5/#32/#76/#77/#78 and is moved before/after value noun in questions, rather than acting as a numeric value. Action literal meanings remain underdetermined; recommend retain named A/B/C/D and translate dependencies confidently.

Clause translations #36–64, using A=[𘓜𗚧 𘀰𘐾 𗙨𗥊], B=[𘓜𗚧 𗀻𘜔 𗙨𗥊], C=[𘓜𗚧 𗤸𘏛 𗦴𗷳], D=[𗳙𗇄 𗥗𗺍 𘓜𗚧], E=execute/perform, R=report, W=wait, Q=𗑝𗘾 coordinator/submitter unknown, Z=𘒷𘕾 𘏛𗩚 'other agents' probable, n1=𗡏𗘁. #36 Request E list(A, B=n1, C, [𗳙𗇄 𘓜𗚧 𗥗𗺍 𗥗𗺍]); assert agent6 E A. #38 Assert B [𗣡𗙂 requires/depends-on] (A done); request agent7 E A. #40 Assert [my P] agrees; request Q submit list(A,B,C,D); assert agent1 E A; request Z W. #42 Assert I agree; assert agent2 E A; request Z W. #44 Request agent3 E list(A,B,C,[𘓜𗚧 𗥗𗺍 𗳙𗇄 𗸶𘓚]); request Z W. #45 Assert agent3 E A; request Z W. #47 Assert A done; assert [𗺍𘂚 𗙨𗥊] = 𗄭𗸊; request agent3 E B. #48 Request agent1 E (B=n1); request agent1 report 𘀰𗘾 [result]; assert agent0 W. #49 Assert (agent1 E A) failed; assert agent1 [𗞘𗄭 try/propose] B; request Z W. #50 Question to agent3: A done? #51 Assert (agent6 E A) failed; request agent3 E B; assert agent6 W. #52 Assert (agent7 [𘍨𗥣 submit] A) failed; request agent3 [try] A; assert agent7 W. #53 Assert [𗺍𘂚 𗙨𗥊] = 𗄭𗸊; assert agent3 E B; request Z W. #55 Assert (agent2 E A) [𗞍𗘠 unknown status]; assert agent2 [try] A; request Z W. #57 Assert agent4 W. #58 Assert (agent1 E B) done; request agent3 E C; request Z W. #59 Assert B done; assert [𗺍𘂚 𗙨𗥊] = 𗷋𘎱; assert agent3 E C; request Z W. #60 Request agent3 E C; request agent3 report result; request Z W. #61 Assert agent6 [𗙴𗦛 confirms/knows?] (B done); request agent3 E C; assert agent6 W. #62 Assert (agent2 E B) failed; assert agent2 W; request agent3 report result. #63 Assert agent5 W. #64 C done; [𗺍𘂚 𗙨𗥊]=𗄭𗸊; agent3 E D; request Z W.
